To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
pregnancy and 3-alpha-hydroxy-diol progesterone (3-alpha-OH-DHP) have no effect on aortic depresser nerve activity in rats.
3 alpha-O-H-DHP, a major metabolite progesterone, mimics the effects that pregnancy has on baroreflex function.

1) pregnancy and 3alpha-OH-DHP do not affect baroreceptor discharge, 2) the baroreceptor curve is shifted to the left in pregnant animals, and 3) 3alpha-OHDHP does not affect baroreflex gain in either virgin or in pregnant animals.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how changes in blood volume and blood pressure during pregnancy are sensed by the baroreceptors.
the mechanisms by which pregnancy and progesterone metabolites influence cardiovascular regulation.
the effects of pregnancy, progesterone, and its metabolites on the baroreceptor reflex.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the afferent baroceptor response to changes in MAP is similar in virgin and pregnant rats.
3 alpha-OHP does not appear to contribute to afferent barosensitization during pregnancy.

3 alpha-O-H-DHP does not alter baroreceptor discharge, but it does affect the efferent limb of the baroreflex, which may be the primary mechanism by which this metabolite of progsterone alters baroreflex function during pregnancy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
progesterone metabolites do not alter afferent baroceptor discharge in virgin and pregnant rats.
the afferent barosensitive neurons are not affected by pregnancy and 3alpha-hydroxy-diol.
progesterone and/or 3 alpha-OHP may have a direct action on the efferent limb (central nervous system) of the baroreflex and an indirect action on the afferent arm (baroreceptors) of the baro reflex.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the baroreflex function is altered in pregnancy, but that this alteration is not due to a change in baroreceptor sensitivity.
pregnancy and 3-alpha-OH-DHP have no effect on the afferent barosensitivty of the aortic baroreceptors.
pregnancy is associated with a decrease in baroreceptor discharge threshold, but this change is not due to the actions of 3 alpha, 5 beta-THP.
